notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($25,000,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts monetary contributions from businesses, unions and PACs to county commission, sheriff, assessor, treasurer, recorder and clerk candidates, reported to the Secretary of State since 2023. The Secretary of State's export has no contributor type, so organizations are recognized by name (LLC, Inc, PAC, union locals) and some are missed; contributions are matched to candidates by name. Nevada allows business and union contributions. Individuals, in-kind gifts, and party and candidate committees are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-12. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Nevada yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS009094, citing Volatus Aerospace

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS007466, citing Vice News

redFlags.label: Gunshot detection (ShotSpotter)
redFlags.detail: The Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department introduced ShotSpotter gunshot detection in 2017 and expanded the program in 2019 after applying for a $11.5 million grant.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS000213, citing Las Vegas Review Journal

redFlags.label: Real-time crime center
redFlags.detail: The Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department's Technical Operations Section uses gunshot detection technology, face recognition software, social media monitoring and automated license plate readers at its real-time crime center. source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS006573, citing KTNV Las Vegas

redFlags.label: Cell-site simulator

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS004066, citing Vocativ

redFlags.label: Private camera registry

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS004829, citing Las Vegas Website

redFlags.label: License-plate readers

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2023 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included. Residents also pay Clark County.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts monetary contributions from businesses, unions and PACs to candidates for mayor and city council, reported to the Secretary of State since 2023. The Secretary of State's export has no contributor type, so organizations are recognized by name (LLC, Inc, PAC, union locals) and some are missed; contributions are matched to candidates by name. Nevada allows business and union contributions. Individuals, in-kind gifts, and party and candidate committees are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-12. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Nevada yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.detail: The North Las Vegas Police Department has patrol cars equipped with automated license plate readers.
